name: illustrator-question-timer-board
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 28.6 - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, Responsive on
story: A media student drew the card their quiz puts up while the class answers: a kicker, a big clock reading 5:00, a note under it, and an amber bar drawn across the foot at its full length for the time draining away. They also drew three moments and switched them off in the layers panel - the panel going red in the last stretch, a TAUOLLA strip for when the chair holds the clock, and an AIKA plate for the moment it runs out. Layers named the way docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md section 5b tells them to, exported with Illustrator's dialog untouched, so Responsive stayed ticked and the file carries a viewBox and no width or height.
idioms: Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build
version="1.1" id="Layer_1" with x="0px" y="0px" and xml:space="preserve" on tab-indented continuation lines
Responsive export: viewBox only, no width/height attributes
<style type="text/css"> holding one property per .stN class, uppercase hex
point type as <text transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 x y)"> with the class list carrying fill, family and size separately
_x20_ escapes with data-name on the two layers whose names carry a space
three hidden layers exported as class="st10" whose rule is display:none - Illustrator's shape for an eye switched off
the drain bar drawn as a bare <rect> at top level rather than inside a group
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: A CLOCK IS THE BEHAVIOUR NOTHING IN THIS CORPUS CARRIED. Section 3 says a layer whose sample reads as M:SS may be bound as a countdown, and section 5b now says a timer is one of the behaviours a drawn graphic can carry - so this file is where both promises are measured together on artwork somebody drew. Four things meet here. The clock layer has to arrive as a bindable countdown rather than as plain text, or the operator gets a field that types over a ticking readout. The drain bar is drawn at full length, which is the vote board's own rule reaching a second behaviour, and it is a bare <rect> rather than a group, so the picker has to offer shapes as well as groups. The three moment layers are switched off the way Illustrator writes it - a display:none class, not an attribute - so an importer reading only the attribute form loses all three silently. And the card is played once per question with new words each time, so its boxes stay as drawn and the text fits inside them rather than the panel growing.
